page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head centred at the top, page number at the top right. No marginal notes. Catchword "in hac" at the lower right, below the last line.

main_text.p: latione divinarum legum, promissionū & comminationum cum hominū factis totaq; vita, [illegible, ~8 letters] colliguntur.
Michaeas revelatione divina edoctus, Achabo Israelitarum Regi, bellum Syriae Regi inferenti, cladem exercitus & inte-ritum praenunciavit. 3.Reg.22.23.

At nunc multi cordati homines, impietatem & iniusticiam hominum aspicientes, & divinas comminationes perpendentes, profspicienter κατανυκτικῶς[?] colligunt, mundum poenas esse daturum. Nec difficile est Prophetas & historiam sacram veteris Testamenti legentibus, & omnia illa cum nostris temporibus moribusque conferentibus, colligere [illegible, ~6 letters], quid de genere humano sit futu-rum. Non enim nudis illi dubiisque coniecturis agunt, sed exempla vitae ad le-gum & promissionum divinarum canones exigunt, & recte facta, praemia: scelera autem, poenas secuturas, certò pronunciant.
4. Pathognomica, κατ' ἀνάλυσιν[?], ab eventibus ad antecedentes causas animum revocant. Ut quum videmus, quam tristis & turbulenta sit Ecclesiae ταραχὴ[?]

page.notes: The running head and "CAP. I" are as printed; the V in HABACVC is read as a vowel U. The page number is printed at the top right and looks like "31", but the last figure is unclear. The Greek words on the page are hard to read: "κατανυκτικῶς" and "κατ' ἀνάλυσιν" are conjectures, the word after "colligere" is unreadable, and the first word of the Greek line near the end of the page is uncertain. Some hyphens at line ends may be printer's hyphens; "inte-ritum", "le-gum" and "futu-rum" are kept as they appear. The text "edoctus" is printed with a long s and read as "edoctus"; "promissionū" uses a macron for the omitted n. The catchword is "in hac".
